thread:
Maya: Ok team — starting a thread to map cross-team dependencies for the Q3 Dedicated launch. We need a view of the critical path and any blockers that will force scope changes. Can folks drop top-3 dependencies and estimated lead times?

Andre: +1. I'll start:
```
- Runtime readiness: kernel selection + quant path (2-4w)
- Model packaging: 8-bit quant tests + compat matrix (3w)
- API feature parity: streaming + tool-calls e2e (2w)
```
Noting runtime and model bits need to land before the canary.

Liam: Infra perspective:
- GPU pool provisioning (dedicated nodes): 3w (procurement + infra templates)
- Autoscale policies + cost guardrails: 2w
- Network/VPC peering for Private customers if we test in VPC: 1w
We need capacity estimate from product for QPS to size pools.

Sophia: SRE/launch criteria notes:
- SLA targets defined (p95 latency, error budget) — need product to sign off
- Runbook + rollback playbook (canary fail conditions) — 1w to draft
- Observability: token-level cost traces + per-model latency dashboards — 2w
Also: who owns post-launch oncall for Dedicated?

Carl: From Product Ops / PM ops:
- Customer asks prioritized: onboarding enterprise X requires private networking + KMS; this sits behind Private but may affect Dedicated cadence if we promised integration.
- Launch criteria proposal: must pass 3 pilot customers + automated regressions for quality and latency.
- We should sequence milestones: feature-complete -> pilot -> GA.
Link to roadmap doc: https://docs.redwood/example/q3-dedicated-roadmap (placeholder)

Maya: Pulling these together: critical path looks like
```
1) infra capacity + autoscale (Liam)
2) runtime + quant kernels (Andre)
3) model packaging + evals (Research)
4) observability + SLA + runbooks (Sophia)
5) pilot customers + docs (Carl/Product)
```
If any of 1-3 slips, GA date moves. Which tasks have parallel work we can do to shave time?

Andre: We can run quant experiments in parallel with kernel integration — Research can hand validated checkpoints to Runtime earlier. That cuts ~1w if we coordinate.

Liam: I can parallelize autoscale policy work with node provisioning. Need an infra owner to finalize capacity numbers by EOD Friday. @Carl can you confirm expected QPS for pilot?

Carl: For pilot A we expect ~40 qps steady with 120 peak. Pilot B is smaller. I'll put numbers in the doc and tag this thread.

Sophia: Also flagging that e2e load tests need a staging harness that mirrors Dedicated networking. That's 1w to set up unless we reuse the existing stress cluster.

Maya: Action items from this thread:
- Carl: confirm pilot QPS + pilot customer list (due: Thu)
- Liam: infra capacity plan + owner for provisioning (due: Fri)
- Andre: timeline for quant + kernel integration and any blockers (due: Fri)
- Research: pre-validated quant checkpoints (due: Tue)
- Sophia: draft runbook + staging load harness options (due: Mon)
I'll consolidate into a dependency map and share a Gantt tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Reminder — created calendar event \"Q3 Dedicated critical-path sync\" for 2024-03-04 16:00 UTC and invited Maya, Andre, Liam, Sophia, Carl.

Andre: One more ask — if we need to trim scope, suggest deferring non-blocking API surface (advanced routing policies, per-token cost UI) to GA+1. Keep canary minimal but safe.

Maya: Agreed. We'll treat those as follow-on. Thanks all — I'll post the dependency map link here once it's up.

Carl: tagging Sales for pilot commitment confirmation after I update QPS numbers.

Sophia: noted. QPS numbers will also feed SRE runbook thresholds.

Liam: I'll open an infra RFC with estimated costs and node configs. Expect draft in 48h.

Maya: Great. Thread closed for now — will reopen after I post the map. :white_check_mark:
